reason: Visceral infection defines hepatic and splenic/marrow involvement, supporting hepatic, haematologic and infectious_immune primary axes. Cutaneous involvement is not defining for this subtype.
Stationary retinal dysfunction defines ocular disease. A nervous-system ancestor does not establish additional neurologic damage.

Defining skeletal abnormalities support musculoskeletal primary. Developmental delay in 5/13 and ptosis in 9/16 support neurologic and ocular involvement. Common endocrine dysfunction is not established.
The tumour originates in the optic nerve, explicitly assigned to ocular. CNS ancestry and associated NF1 do not independently justify neurologic involvement.
Iris hypoplasia and glaucoma define ocular disease. The hereditary neurological ancestor supplies no evidence of extraocular neurologic damage.

Phosphate dysregulation and defining tendon/periarticular calcinosis support metabolic_endocrine and musculoskeletal primary axes. Cerebral calcification alone does not demonstrate neurologic dysfunction; skin damage is not established.

Retinal dystrophy, obesity and polydactyly justify the primary axes; developmental delay in 2/2 supports neurologic involvement. The cap reasonably prioritizes these over sparsely documented renal and cardiac findings.

Gingival inflammation belongs to gastrointestinal. The broad concept does not establish an infectious, autoimmune or other qualifying immune-mediated diagnosis merely through inflammation or plaque association.
Developmental delay in 5/5 defines neurologic disease. Structural cardiac defects individually affect 2/5, and camptodactyly affects 2/5, supporting cardiovascular and musculoskeletal involvement.
Forebrain malformation defines neurologic disease. Individual extra-neural abnormalities occur in 25% or fewer; their overlapping annotations do not establish organ-level frequencies above 30%.
